transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah, I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about my face. Like, the left side looks crooked to me, messed up somehow. I know that probably sounds weird, but it’s all I can focus on.

At work, I’m a stocker at a warehouse, and I’ll be trying to do orders, but I keep thinking people are looking at it. Same thing when I go to salsa night—like everyone can see it right away. They tell me they don’t notice anything, but I don’t really believe them. It just feels obvious to me.
How much time per day would you say you spend thinking about the way your face looks?

Honestly, it feels like… most of the day. I’ll try to focus on work, like filling orders at the warehouse, and then I catch myself thinking, “Is the left side of my face crooked right now? Can they see it?” And then I lose track of what I was doing.

Same thing if I go to salsa night—like I’m supposed to be paying attention to the music or the steps, but I’m thinking about my face and whether people are noticing. Even when they say they don’t see anything, I keep coming back to it. It’s hard to put an exact number on it, but it’s a lot.
When you’re worried about your face looking crooked, do you do anything like checking it in the mirror, touching it, or trying to fix it in your mind?

Yeah… I do. Mostly at work. Like before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll stop in the bathroom and check my face in the mirror, and then I’ll fix my cap because maybe if it sits right it makes it less noticeable. And I rub at the same spot on my face, like that’s going to change it or something.

Sometimes I mean to just look once, but then I get stuck there. And then I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me again. He thinks I’m just wasting time, but it’s not like I’m in there relaxing. I’m trying to make sure I don’t go back out looking… wrong.
Does worrying about the way your face looks ever make it hard for you to function normally—like at work, in social situations, or in other parts of your life?

Yeah… it does. I mean, at work especially. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed—like I’ll be checking my face or fixing my cap, and then orders pile up or I’m late getting back, and they act like I’m just being lazy.

And outside work too, I guess. I used to play soccer sometimes, and I liked salsa nights, and my family does these gatherings where everybody wants pictures… which, honestly, I hate. My cousin is always taking like a hundred photos, even of food, which I don’t get, but anyway—yeah, I’ve started skipping that stuff. Soccer, salsa nights, family things. It’s easier to just not go than to deal with people looking at me or someone trying to take a picture.
Has this concern about your face affected your personal relationships or the way you feel about yourself overall?

Yeah… I think it has. I don’t really feel good about myself most of the time, and it’s like I’m always trying to avoid situations where someone might notice my face or take a picture.

Like with my family, they do gatherings and my cousin is always pulling out her phone—she’ll take pictures of everything, even like a plate of rice, I don’t know why—and I just don’t want to be caught in one. So I skip those now. And I’ve stopped going to soccer and salsa nights too, which I used to actually enjoy.

And work… I mean, that’s not personal relationships exactly, but I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed dealing with this stuff, checking myself or trying to make sure I look okay before I go back out. So yeah, it’s affected a lot.
